entry.title: Ginzburg-Landau Theory with Elastic Incompatibility Describes the Liquid-G-phase-Crystal State Diagram
entry.summary:
We derive a mechanically consistent Ginzburg-Landau theory for the metastable heterogeneous G state reported in deeply undercooled metallic liquids. The central result is that type-II-like mixed-state physics can emerge structurally with the random internal stress field playing the role of the magnetic field. Frozen eigenstrain due to elastic incompatibility between ordered cores and the amorphous matrix generates incompatible stress, while the non-affine internal strain in the liquid-like matrix in between the ordered cores relaxes that stress over a finite screening length $λ_σ$ (analogous to the London length in the superconducting problem).

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #materials-science #rust

entry.title: GLP Networking API Specification
entry.summary:
Multiagent deterministic GLP (madGLP) runs Grassroots Logic Programs (GLP) as agents that communicate solely by asynchronous message passing, and assumes fair delivery: every message sent is eventually delivered. Each agent runs on a person's smartphone, named by the person's public key. A grassroots platform depends on no global resource but the network, so agents must reach one another over Bluetooth Low Energy, on a local network, and across the Internet from behind NAT, via rendezvous servers anyone can run.

Source: arXiv CS (PL, SE, DB, DC, DS) · Tags: #compilers #distributed-systems #networking #rust

entry.title: Package managers have an integrity problem
entry.summary:
I tested 25 of the most popular package managers to check whether they detect a compromised package repository injecting malicious code into legitimate packages. This code integrity problem could be solved using cryptographic hashes or signatures, but many package managers are still vulnerable to this threat. Of the 25 package managers reviewed 1 , fewer than half used lockfiles that checked for tampering by default, and only two verified the integrity of every package they downloaded.

Source: Trail of Bits Security Research · Tags: #infosec #cryptography #rust #databases

entry.title: Strongly Adaptive Asynchronous Byzantine Agreement with Linear Communication and Almost-Everywhere Termination
entry.summary:
It is well known that Byzantine agreement requires $\Omega(t^2)$ messages against a strongly adaptive adversary that may corrupt $t=\Theta(n)$ parties and suppress a party's undelivered messages upon corruption. We circumvent this lower bound by relaxing termination: for any constant $0<\nu<1$, at least a $(1-\nu)$ fraction of the honest parties terminate, while agreement and validity hold for every honest decision. For every constant corruption gap $\delta>0$ and every $t\leq(1-\delta)n/3$, we construct binary agreement with this guarantee in authenticated asynchronous networks against strongly adaptive corruptions with message takebacks.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #rust #combinatorics

entry.title: The Effects of Generative AI on Collaboration and Social Networks Among Knowledge Workers
entry.summary:
The rapid diffusion of generative artificial intelligence has raised concerns that knowledge work may become less dependent on human-to-human interaction. Yet because AI-generated outputs require interpretation, verification, and social legitimation, generative AI may instead increase collaboration among workers. We test these competing predictions using passively collected behavioral data from more than 12,000 knowledge workers observed over 13 months during the staged organizational rollout of an AI-powered assistant (Microsoft Copilot).

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #rust #clean-tech

entry.title: On "AI Brendans" or "Virtual Brendans". There are now multiple AI performance engineering agents that use or are trained on my work.
entry.summary:
There are now multiple AI performance engineering agents that use or are trained on my work. Some are helper agents that interpret flame graphs or eBPF metrics, sometimes privately called AI Brendan ; others have trained on my work to create a virtual Brendan that claims it can tune everything just like the real thing. These virtual Brendans sound like my brain has been uploaded to the cloud by someone who is now selling it (yikes!).

Source: Brendan Gregg (Systems Performance & eBPF) · Tags: #kernel-os #performance #rust #distributed-systems
